content.comment_body: When I create a program that uses a Softkey, I notice something odd. In [product_name] [article_no] Standard, the program can't be transferred to [article_no].1 and higher versions. Likewise, a program developed in [product_name] [article_no].1 (FS4) [version_no] and [version_no] can't be moved to the standard [article_no] version. The workaround is to delete the Softkey, switch to the other [product_name] version, and then reinsert the Softkey. The way it looks is the same, but what is actually different?
This issue exists in [product_name] [version_no] when using softkeys. You should check a similar discussion in the German section of the forum regarding [product_name] [version_no] error message.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing compatibility issues when transferring programs with the Softkey function between different versions of [product_name] [article_no] hardware using [product_name] [version_no]. Programs created for one hardware revision cannot be directly moved to another, and users have to manually remove and re-add the Softkey to complete the transfer. This shows there are version-dependent inconsistencies in how the software interacts with different hardware revisions, disrupting the workflow.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward program transfers with Softkey functionality between all [product_name] [article_no] hardware versions, seeking consistent operation regardless of the specific [article_no] revision.
